title: German audiences expect Africans
summary: Audiences expected savages and could not believe the band were Americans; they gave seventy sold-out performances.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: But tell me about the -- you know, your arrival in Berlin. Had there been advertising -- were people expecting you?
I mean, this was something new. They hadn't had a black show.

It was something new and it was something like that occasion in Copenhagen that happened. Some of them were waiting to see gorillas and baboons and everything. They didn't know what they were going to see. Well, when these guys come at that time, because they didn't -- they didn't see no bad looking guys, because everybody had (Congolene) on their hair and everybody -- and they couldn't believe that we were Africans. See, some of them said, 'Well they must be from Brazil or some other place. They can't be Africans.' Course, all of the idea they had of American blacks was that they had kinky hair and a big flat nose and big thick lips.
So they didn't know what to think. But, one thing, I think we did something like seventy something performances in Berlin. And everyone packed to the door.
